framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: High-risk systems must comply with the Section 2 requirements taking account of intended purpose and the generally acknowledged state of the art, with the Art. 9 risk management system taken into account.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Notified-body certificates are valid for the period stated, at most five years for Annex I systems and four years for Annex III systems, extendable at the provider's request after re-assessment; where a system no longer meets Section 2 requirements the body must, applying proportionality, suspend, withdraw or restrict the certificate unless the provider takes corrective action within the deadline set by the body.

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Systemic-risk GPAI providers must assess and mitigate systemic risks at Union level, track and report serious incidents to the AI Office, and ensure adequate cybersecurity for the model and its physical infrastructure.
what_is_tested: Systemic risk assessment/mitigation; incident reporting; cybersecurity

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
clause_or_page: Objectives, point A; EC Code page
requirement_paraphrase: The Code is a voluntary tool for demonstrating compliance with Arts. 53 and 55 and states that adherence is not conclusive evidence of compliance; the Commission and AI Board have confirmed it as an adequate voluntary tool.
what_is_tested: Compliance demonstration route for GPAI providers

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories obtain assurance that security mitigations meet the Security Goal through independent external security reviews where internal expertise is inadequate, frequent red-teaming of network and physical access management, competitive bug bounties for public-facing endpoints, periodic personnel integrity testing, third-party security reporting channels, endpoint/intrusion detection tools and a security incident response team.
what_is_tested: Security assurance testing of model and infrastructure
who_tests: Signatory provider; independent external security reviewers

requirement_paraphrase: Recommends AI-specific penetration testing of AI system components before deployment and periodically afterwards, including testing outputs and system behaviour.
what_is_tested: Exploitable cybersecurity weaknesses in AI components and behaviour

framework: Singapore IMDA Starter Kit for Testing LLM-Based Applications for Safety and Reliability (v1.0, January 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Content red teaming probes the app dynamically for blind spots, multi-turn failures and subjective harms; define targeted vs open-ended objectives; use domain experts, AI experts and target end users with diversity; track acceptable response rate, refusal rate and turns-to-unsafe; annotators may be red teamers, independent third parties or LLM judges with human sampling; automated red teaming (e.g. PAIR, Crescendo-style) is an emerging complement.
who_tests: Developers/deployers, domain experts, independent annotators, automated tools

framework: Abu Dhabi Law No. (3) of 2024 establishing the AI and Advanced Technology Council
requirement_paraphrase: The Council sets the conditions, controls, standards and systems that must be observed in AI investment and research, and follows the performance and feasibility of AI-related policies. The law gives no explicit power to test AI systems.
what_is_tested: None directly (policies and standards-setting; performance of policies)

framework: Dubai AI Integration Matrix Framework for Government Organizations (Dubai Digital Authority, August 2025, Version 1.0 per front matter; earlier listing date 28 Apr 2026 conflicts)
clause_or_page: Ch. 10.3 (AI Ethics Policy) and 10.2 (Initiative Approval), printed p. 87
requirement_paraphrase: States that every AI initiative under DDA must demonstrate alignment with DDA's ethical principles and undergo rigorous validation for ethical compliance across its lifecycle, and passes a standard approval workflow including technical feasibility, business case, risk evaluation and resource sign-off.
what_is_tested: Ethical compliance validation; initiative risk evaluation

framework: UAE National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, Version 1.1 (UAE Cyber Security Council, November 2025; v1.0 September 2025)
clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.4.4 (s2.4 Operational Security), printed p.14
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must secure its AI/ML systems through comprehensive testing and validation that gives assurance of their resilience against potential threats.
what_is_tested: Security and resilience of AI/ML systems against threats
who_tests: The entity in scope under s1.2: ministries and federal authorities and non-government CII entities; for emirate government entities verifiers read s1.2 differently (directly only where no emirate CIIP programme exists, or directly or through the Emirate Lead). See UAE-Federal-P3-08.

framework: US NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1, January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Identify and document scientific integrity and TEVV considerations, including experimental design, data collection/selection (representativeness, suitability), system trustworthiness and construct validation.
what_is_tested: Validity of test design and data
